newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus Communications says to acquire Optus Vision.
newsitem.headline: Optus Communications says to acquire Optus Vision.

text.p: Telecommunicatiions carrier Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Friday it had reached an agreement to acquire 100 percent of pay television and telephone company Optus Vision.

In return for transferring their shares to Optus, each of the other partners in Optus Vision has been issued a convertible note which can be converted to shares in Optus Communications at or after the company's initial public offering, Optus Communications said in a statement.

Shareholders in Optus Vision are Optus Communications and Continental Cablevision Inc, owned by American telephone concern US West Inc, with 46.5 percent each, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd at five percent and the Kerry Stokes-controlled Seven Network Ltd at two percent.

Under the agreement, Continental Cablevision will continue to provide technical support and expertise to Optus Vision for the launch of a local telephone service over the Optus Vision network, Optus Communications said.
Optus Communications shareholder, Mayne Nickeless Ltd, a health and transport company, has agreed to underwrite incentives to US West for these services, Optus Communnications said.
In return Mayne Nickless will be allotted additional shares in Optus Communications, increasing its stake to 26.1 percent, Optus Communications said.
The parties are released from current litigation and any future claims as a result of the agreement, Optus Communications said.
Seven has been suing other shareholders for alleged breaches last August in the Optus Vision shareholders' agreement.

Seven claims Optus Communications, US West and Publishing and Broadcasting were breaching the shareholders' agreement when they agreed to grant options which would increase Publishing and Broadcasting's stake in Optus Vision.

"It has always been our intention to maximise availability of communications services to Australians under one brand and we are now extremely well placed to deliver virtually all needs of residential business and government sectors," Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said in the statement.
Ownership structures of Optus Vision's affiliated companies Sportsvision and Movievision and their respective programmning agreements were unaffected by Friday's agreement, Optus Communications said.
Transfer of ownership is expected to be completed by the end of next month and is subject to approval by Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board, Optus Communications said.
Optus Vision has 180,000 pay television customers across Australia, Optus Communications said.
